How about your bank account? That's in the cloud too. How do you move that offline?


Elizabeth Holmes (@ElizabethHolmes)

Delete your search history, delete your bookmarks, delete your reddit, medical records, 12 yr old tumblr, delete everything.

Every photo on the cloud, every message on every platform.

None of it is safe. 

It will all become public in the next year
Local storage and compute 📈

there is no safe future that includes continued capability improvements in open source models.

Trump's war is going to make Iran very very rich


John Ridge (@WeaponScientist)

Approximately 32,000 vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz in 2023. 

Assuming similar volume, a notional $2M toll per vessel would net Iran ~$64B annually. 

That is nearly double Iran’s total revenue of $34B from oil exports in 2024.



— https://nitter.net/WeaponScientist/status/2041677554721886371#m

"Militarily dominate the world"


Harlan Stewart (@HumanHarlan)

Anthropic is trying to prevent its powerful new AI from being used in dangerous ways, but the most dangerous use (by a wide margin) is the one Anthropic itself has planned.

The planned use—and why they made it to begin with—is to accelerate the creation of superhumanly powerful AI agents, by automating the R&D process. This plan is not a secret.

They believe they are on track to create a "a country of geniuses in a data center" t

Iran won this war


Adam Schwarz (@AdamJSchwarz)

The NYT is reporting that Iran, in addition to gaining administrative control over the Strait of Hormuz, will now charge $2m per ship for safe passage, which it will split with Oman.

It was free pre-war.

Trump & Netanyahu have increased Iranian leverage over the global economy.



— https://nitter.net/AdamJSchwarz/status/2041666296325066901#m
You know those 1950s science fiction stories where astronauts come back from a space voyage to find that the entire Earth has been destroyed in a nuclear war?
I suppose there’s no rule that says you have to put the houses and hotels on the color strips in Monopoly, but I feel like if you put them anywhere else on the property, you’d be a psychopath.

While we were dyeing eggs this year, my math-loving child wanted to write the quadratic formula on one. 

ME: Wow, it’s been a long time since I’ve had to use the quadratic formula. How do you use it again?

KID: (Starts explaining it to me, gets frustrated) Look — it’s all on the egg.
You do hear weird stories about the craft service table on that show.

As I get more interested in bargain shopping in my late middle age I find myself in more stores where the Muzak is heavy on songs I mostly know from comedians and comedy writers slightly older than me making fun of them.

Like, before this morning, I had never actually heard “Forever in Bluejeans.”
“But … but … I was glowering!”
Turns out I was right! But, Donnie, I bet you can beat that!
What the hell, let’s really go for it and spell the word “bbookkeeppeerr”!
Red Sox win first game of the season! Pennant Fever grips Hub!
No! I’m no weirdo! I dip mine in the toilet water.
Smuckers would have thrown a parade!
I have a memory of George W. Bush being at 25% approval by, like, 2008. Was he really that low or was that a bit of schadenfreudic wishful thinking on my part?

Gene Shalit is a hundred!

Or should that be a pun-dred?

Talk about long-gene-ity!

Shal-it be a happy birthday or not worth one red centenarian?

parade.com/news/today-s...

I was thinking about this old Spider-Man comic from the late 70s. Since the Marvel Universe operates on a “sliding” continuity time-wise this story probably now takes place maybe 10 years ago, presumably with the 2016 SNL cast. “Moynihan! No! That Drunk Uncle’s for real!”
@bibbymoynihan.bsky.social
I think you’re a hunk-a hunk-a burning shit.

Can we slow down a bit?

McDonald’s all-day breakfast lasted from 2015-2020. 2020 was also when Walmart stopped being 24 hours. 

Sierra Mist was discontinued in 2023. 

I know a lot changed with Covid but it was 6 years ago, not 50.

Pizza Hut buffets do seem ancient but those might be coming back!
This is the joke that was quite popular online and which Vulture/Splitsider called “inexcusable.” www.vulture.com/2012/03/snl-...

With the passing of Mr. Norris, I’m going to honor great American tradition by making it all about myself and sharing this image of the most successful of the five total jokes I wrote that got onto Weekend Update when I was a freelance joke submitter.
I told you this would end badly. In retrospect, there were signs that Trump was not a good leader.

Salarymen, specialists, and small businesses
How Japan has changed in the last 20 years
Maybe you should have bought an electric car. The Iran War is illustrating the cost of anti-EV nonsense.
Plentiful, high-paying jobs in the age of AI
AI has the worst sales pitch I've ever seen. "Our product will make you economically useless, and possibly kill you" is not a value proposition.
The economic consequences of the Iran war. The U.S. is likely to get off easy, while others will bear the brunt.
There isn't always a "long arc" of morality. Progressives should beware the idea that history will deliver them inevitable victories.
A conversation with Claude. In which a robot and I have a fun dorm-room chat about the future of science.
China is quietly looking weaker. Xi Jinping's paranoia, rapidly changing technology, and the limitations of China's system could cut short the Chinese Century.
Save us, Digital Cronkite!. Social media tore our society apart. Perhaps AI can put it back together.
